# Rosemary West

## Appearance

Rosemary is a tall, fair woman who maintains a remarkably youthful look. She has golden hair, rosy cheeks, and calm, heavenly blue eyes. She dresses stylishly and possesses a STATELY, queen-like presence.

_Sources: [v5 c4 P52](../source/v05-c04.md#nw-v05-c04-p0052), [v5 c13 P7](../source/v05-c13.md#nw-v05-c13-p0007), [v5 c13 P9](../source/v05-c13.md#nw-v05-c13-p0009), [v5 c14 P39](../source/v05-c14.md#nw-v05-c14-p0039), [v5 c20 P9](../source/v05-c20.md#nw-v05-c20-p0009), [v5 c21 P14](../source/v05-c21.md#nw-v05-c21-p0014)_

## Personality

Rosemary is universally regarded as a sweet, brave, and forgiving woman. She carries a gracious, placid demeanor along with a stately dignity that earns her respect rather than dislike. She possesses an attitude of delighted surprise toward life that makes her seem youthful to everyone she meets. Highly compassionate and maternal, she listens sympathetically without judgment or ridicule.

_Sources: [v5 c12 P5](../source/v05-c12.md#nw-v05-c12-p0005), [v5 c13 P9](../source/v05-c13.md#nw-v05-c13-p0009), [v5 c20 P9](../source/v05-c20.md#nw-v05-c20-p0009), [v5 c20 P14](../source/v05-c20.md#nw-v05-c20-p0014), [v5 c20 P16](../source/v05-c20.md#nw-v05-c20-p0016), [v5 c21 P6](../source/v05-c21.md#nw-v05-c21-p0006)_

## History

Rosemary West grew up in a traditional Episcopalian household at the old homestead on the hill near Glen St. Mary. When she was seventeen, she was engaged to Martin Crawford, who drowned when his ship was wrecked at the Magdalens. Following her mother's death on Rosemary's twenty-fifth birthday, her grief-stricken sister Ellen persuaded her to swear on their mother's Bible that she would never marry. Rosemary lived quietly with Ellen for ten years, staying close to home and eventually offering music lessons to local children. Her life shifted when she encountered the Presbyterian minister, John Meredith, by a hidden spring in Rainbow Valley; the two formed a swift, deep connection over shared interests in books and music. When John proposed, Rosemary felt forced by her solemn oath to turn him down by letter, causing both of them deep sorrow. Months later, Norman Douglas persuaded Ellen to release Rosemary from her vow so that Ellen herself could marry Norman. After Una Meredith came to ask Rosemary to marry her father, Rosemary sent John a letter requesting to meet at the spring, leading to their reconciliation and upcoming double wedding alongside Ellen and Norman.

_Sources: [v5 c2 P66](../source/v05-c02.md#nw-v05-c02-p0066), [v5 c13 P0](../source/v05-c13.md#nw-v05-c13-p0000), [v5 c13 P5](../source/v05-c13.md#nw-v05-c13-p0005), [v5 c13 P19](../source/v05-c13.md#nw-v05-c13-p0019), [v5 c21 P15](../source/v05-c21.md#nw-v05-c21-p0015), [v5 c21 P17](../source/v05-c21.md#nw-v05-c21-p0017), [v5 c21 P24](../source/v05-c21.md#nw-v05-c21-p0024), [v5 c21 P28](../source/v05-c21.md#nw-v05-c21-p0028), [v5 c22 P21](../source/v05-c22.md#nw-v05-c22-p0021), [v5 c22 P41](../source/v05-c22.md#nw-v05-c22-p0041), [v5 c32 P12](../source/v05-c32.md#nw-v05-c32-p0012), [v5 c32 P13](../source/v05-c32.md#nw-v05-c32-p0013), [v5 c34 P13](../source/v05-c34.md#nw-v05-c34-p0013), [v5 c34 P24](../source/v05-c34.md#nw-v05-c34-p0024), [v5 c34 P44](../source/v05-c34.md#nw-v05-c34-p0044), [v5 c35 P0](../source/v05-c35.md#nw-v05-c35-p0000)_

## Background by volume

- Distant relative of Leslie West  <sub>[v5 c2 P66](../source/v05-c02.md#nw-v05-c02-p0066)</sub>
- Lost her father at age three and her twelve-year-old brother five years later  <sub>[v5 c21 P15](../source/v05-c21.md#nw-v05-c21-p0015)</sub>
- Her teenage sweetheart, Martin Crawford, was drowned in a shipwreck  <sub>[v5 c2 P66](../source/v05-c02.md#nw-v05-c02-p0066), [v5 c13 P0](../source/v05-c13.md#nw-v05-c13-p0000)</sub>
- Made a solemn vow on her mother's Bible to her sister Ellen never to marry  <sub>[v5 c21 P23](../source/v05-c21.md#nw-v05-c21-p0023), [v5 c21 P24](../source/v05-c21.md#nw-v05-c21-p0024)</sub>

## Quotes

> I—I came for a drink  <sub>[v5 c13 P11](../source/v05-c13.md#nw-v05-c13-p0011)</sub>

> Will you let me have it? You made it so knackily. I never saw anyone make a birch cup so since my little brother used to make them long ago—before he died.  <sub>[v5 c13 P15](../source/v05-c13.md#nw-v05-c13-p0015)</sub>

> It is calm to-night. If there were a wind it would blow your breath away. We get ‘a’ the airts the wind can blow’ up here. This place should be called Four Winds instead of the Harbour.  <sub>[v5 c13 P22](../source/v05-c13.md#nw-v05-c13-p0022)</sub>

> Nonsense. You see a beau for me in every bush, Ellen. Why he told me all about his wife to-night—how much she was to him—how empty her death had left the world.  <sub>[v5 c13 P33](../source/v05-c13.md#nw-v05-c13-p0033)</sub>

> No, I wouldn’t laugh inside, either. Why should I? Something has hurt you—it never amuses me to see anybody hurt, no matter what hurts them. If you feel that you’d like to tell me what has hurt you I’ll be glad to listen. But if you think you’d rather not—that’s all right, too, dear.  <sub>[v5 c20 P16](../source/v05-c20.md#nw-v05-c20-p0016)</sub>
